chats.answer:
For a full remote workday off-grid with a Starlink Mini + MacBook, I'd recommend a portable power station with at least 1,000Wh of battery capacity. That should cover roughly 2 working days without solar, depending on your MacBook and how heavily you use it.

If you're planning to work remotely for 3–5 days, a 2,000Wh power station or a smaller station paired with solar panels makes more sense.

4. How to extend your battery life

For this setup, the most important detail is how you connect your Starlink Mini.

Starlink specifies a 100W USB-C PD supply (20V/5A) when using its USB-C-to-barrel cable. A 65W USB-C port isn't sufficient under its published requirements. 
Starlink Help Center
+1

To maximize runtime, power the MacBook through USB-C and the Starlink Mini through a compatible 100W USB-C output or DC adapter. Avoid leaving the AC inverter running unnecessarily.

A 200W solar panel could replenish roughly 500–800Wh on a good sunny day, potentially covering your daily consumption. Actual production depends on weather, shading, panel orientation, and location.

My pick: The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 for weekend remote work, or the EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max if you need several days without charging.

A 2,000Wh model is a better choice if you want to work for several days without recharging.

Two things that make a big difference

Use DC/USB-C power where possible. Starlink specifies a 100W USB-C PD source supporting 20V/5A with its compatible cable. That is a power-source rating, not continuous consumption.

+1
 If you need two USB-C outputs, check the station's individual port ratings before buying.

Add a 200W solar panel for longer trips. In good sunlight, it may replenish roughly 500–800Wh daily, potentially enough to sustain this setup indefinitely on sunny days. Cloud cover, shading, and seasonal sunlight can reduce this significantly.
